behavior: Resume an interrupted agent-harness workflow from its latest PostgreSQL checkpoint after process kill, and persist human interrupt requests so a 24h-simulated delayed approval continues the run with equivalent evidence.
nonGoals: No initial checkpoint persistence (HAR-003-T01); this task assumes checkpoints already land at each node boundary
No adapter, transport or evidence code path changes
No planning, requirement or catalog edits
commands: STRUCTILE_DEV_POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE="$PWD/.local/postgres-password" docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.test.yaml up -d --wait postgres

STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_HOST=127.0.0.1 STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PORT=55432 STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_USER=structile STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_DB=structile STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE="$PWD/.local/postgres-password" node --test packages/agent-harness/test/*.test.ts
notes: protectedTests HAR-002 is the catalog suite covering HAR-003, HAR-004, HAR-005, HAR-006 and HAR-010 (verification/test-catalog.json); per CP-002's ruling this suite will be re-cut into per-requirement sub-suites, and this contract cites the current catalog entry pending that amendment. runnerDigest is the attested G0 runner image pending a G1 runner attestation; task-ready v1 does not verify runnerDigest or testSourceDigest. testSourceDigest is the oracle-input digest of structile-conformance main 46c8cf99cbac5d0c87729e08db20bbadbe2bacd0, computed by calling the runner's own runnerDigests() in src/evidence.ts directly rather than invented. Depends on HAR-003-T01 landing first: this task assumes the PostgreSQL checkpointer and its pg client dependency already exist in packages/agent-harness/package.json; it adds no new dependency itself, only src/test changes within the existing allowedPaths. compose.yaml's postgres service publishes no host port and sits only on the internal `data` network, so a host-run `node --test` process has no route to it; the compose step now layers the repo-root test-only override compose.test.yaml (`-f compose.yaml -f compose.test.yaml`), which publishes postgres on 127.0.0.1:55432 without changing compose.yaml's own security posture, and is still postgres-service-only/detached rather than the whole-stack `docker compose up --build --wait` the README documents. Tests reach PostgreSQL via STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_HOST=127.0.0.1 and STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PORT=55432, plus STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_USER/STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_DB (fixed values from compose.yaml) and STRUCTILE_POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE pointed at the same local secret file used to bring the container up; all four are set explicitly on the `node --test` command line. This sequence was executed end-to-end against a live Docker daemon on 2026-08-25: compose up -d --wait postgres over the override reached Healthy, and a host client authenticated to 127.0.0.1:55432 as structile/structile and ran SELECT 1 successfully before teardown. Separately, runnerDigest carries the attested G0 runner image digest because no G1 runner digest exists yet: the protected G1 workflow builds the image fresh from Containerfile and computes imageDigest from the built image, and conformance src/ and verification/ have grown substantially since the G0 authority commit, so the G1 image's digest will differ. task-ready v1 verifies neither digest, but readiness against a real protected run requires the pinned runner to match, so this field is a placeholder to be re-pinned to the first attested G1 runner digest. Every task contract merged to date carries the same placeholder. 2026-08-26 touch-up: protectedTests re-pointed to HARD-001 per the CP-002 re-cut now merged into verification/test-catalog.json, testSourceDigest re-pinned at structile-conformance main 20ca0d3, and baseCommit bumped to structile main 5dda0d5, retiring the stale-baseCommit task-ready violations this contract previously carried.
